title: Microsoft Azure Database Administrator Associate DP-300

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.

nodes.title: Azure SQL Database — Match the Pair
Mixed exam topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Some exam objectives don't fit neatly into a single domain — they span protocols, tools, or concepts covered briefly in multiple sections. These cards treat each item as a stand-alone fact, the way an exam question presents it: one concept, one answer.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a hub, a switch, and a router?
flashcards.back: Hub: Layer 1, repeats every frame to all ports — all devices share bandwidth, collisions guaranteed. Switch: Layer 2, forwards frames using a MAC address table to only the destination port — full duplex, no collisions, each port gets full bandwidth. Router: Layer 3, makes forwarding decisions based on IP address, connects different networks. Hub is legacy; switches dominate LAN; routers are at network edges.

flashcards.front: What is RAID 5 and how many drives can it tolerate losing?
flashcards.back: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across at least 3 drives. Any single drive failure can be recovered by reconstructing missing data from the remaining drives and parity. It cannot tolerate 2 simultaneous drive failures. Effective capacity = (N-1) × drive size. Read performance is excellent; write requires parity recalculation. RAID 6 tolerates 2 failures using double parity.

flashcards.front: What does a proxy server do, and how does a forward proxy differ from a reverse proxy?
flashcards.back: Forward proxy: sits between clients and the internet on behalf of clients — used for content filtering, caching, and anonymizing outbound requests (the server sees the proxy's IP). Reverse proxy: sits in front of servers on behalf of the server — used for load balancing, SSL termination, caching, and hiding backend topology (the client sees the proxy's IP). Both intermediate HTTP, but they protect opposite sides.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network architecture?
flashcards.back: A demilitarized zone is a network segment between the untrusted internet and the trusted internal network, typically protected by two firewalls (or two interfaces on one firewall). Public-facing services (web, email, DNS) sit in the DMZ: internet can reach them but not the internal network; if the DMZ host is compromised, the inner firewall still blocks access to the internal LAN.

questions.q: Two Azure SQL Databases are deployed to a primary region and a secondary region for disaster recovery. The application uses a single read/write listener endpoint and must continue working after an automatic regional failover without any connection-string changes. Which feature provides this?
choices: Point-in-time restore to a new server
questions.explanation: An auto-failover group on Azure SQL Database provides listener endpoints (a read/write listener and a read-only listener) plus an automatic failover policy across regions, so applications connect to a stable DNS name and continue to work after Azure fails the group over. Plain active geo-replication exposes per-database secondary endpoints and only supports manual failover. Zone redundancy protects within a single region, not across regions. PITR is a backup-restore feature, not a failover mechanism.

questions.q: A DBA must ensure a single Azure SQL Database can survive a full region outage with an RPO measured in seconds and automatic redirect of the application after failover. Which configuration meets this?
choices: Zone-redundant configuration within the same region only.
An auto-failover group with a readable secondary in a paired region and a read-write listener endpoint.
Weekly geo-restore from backups to the paired region.
Long-term retention (LTR) backups stored in geo-redundant storage.
questions.explanation: An auto-failover group replicates asynchronously to a secondary in another region (RPO of seconds) and provides read-write/read-only listener endpoints so the app follows the failover automatically. Zone redundancy protects against datacenter (not region) loss, geo-restore and LTR are recovery mechanisms with far larger RPO/RTO and no automatic endpoint redirect.

questions.q: You must migrate an on-premises SQL Server database to Azure with minimal code changes. The application depends on SQL Server Agent jobs, cross-database queries, CLR assemblies, and Service Broker. Which Azure database target should you choose?
choices: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server
questions.explanation: Azure SQL Managed Instance is the PaaS option with the highest compatibility with on-premises SQL Server. It supports SQL Server Agent, cross-database queries within the instance, CLR, Service Broker, Database Mail, and most other instance-scoped features. Azure SQL Database (single database) is database-scoped and lacks SQL Agent and cross-database queries. Cosmos DB is a different NoSQL engine. Azure Database for MySQL is a different RDBMS entirely.

questions.q: An elastic pool hosts 50 databases with spiky, uncorrelated workloads. One database occasionally consumes most of the pool's eDTUs and starves the others. Which control limits a single database's impact?
choices: Move every database to its own dedicated database immediately.
Set per-database min/max eDTU (or vCore) caps within the pool so no single database can monopolize resources.
Delete the noisy database from the pool.
questions.explanation: Elastic pools support per-database resource min/max settings; capping the maximum eDTU/vCore per database prevents any one database from consuming the whole pool and starving neighbors, while a per-database minimum guarantees a floor. Splitting all 50 into single databases defeats the cost benefit of pooling, deleting the database is not a resourcing control, and pools do not rely on the auto-scaling toggle described.
